title: Northern Lakes Transmission Operations and the Upper Midwest Reliability Coordinator: severe geomagnetic storm
summary: A fictional high-latitude transmission operator (345 kV system, GIC monitors on 9 autotransformers, holdover clocks) and its reliability coordinator, with an exercise generated from their simulated plans: a G4 to G5 geomagnetic storm after a coronal mass ejection, with a NERC-style operating procedure applied ahead of the Kp conditions, rising neutral currents, a transformer gas alarm and GNSS time degradation.
notice: EXERCISE MATERIAL — for training use. Northern Lakes Transmission Operations, the reliability coordinator, their people, customers and sites are simulated; NOAA-style products in the exercise are marked as exercise products; the public sources consulted for realism are listed in reference/grid-geomagnetic-storm/SOURCES.md.

scenarios.title: Aurora Over Texas
scenarios.summary: After an X-class flare and a fast CME, a geomagnetic storm reaches G5 over about 18 hours; NLTO must apply its GMD procedure ahead of the Kp conditions, watch neutral currents and a transformer gas alarm, handle GNSS time degradation, and keep its messages and the reliability coordinator's consistent.
